solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Recently defeated, crushed by online extremists?

indicators.note: the defeated word is squeezed between the letters that follow, as if crushed
the extremists of online are its outermost letters, first and last

parts.note: flat as in deflated, beaten down, defeated

explanation.surface: A recent loss, blamed on fanatics who rant on the internet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crushed by' puts FLAT between O and E, the ends that 'extremists' takes from 'online'.
explanation.definitionFit: An adverbial phrase meaning lately, in the recent past.

clue.text: Drink or brawl, ultimately promoted with Italian backing

indicators.note: the final letter of the brawl word is lifted higher up the down entry

parts.note: a fracas is a noisy brawl

indicators.note: backing means the abbreviation runs backwards in the grid

explanation.surface: A choice between a drink and a fight, with some Italian support thrown in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately promoted' moves the last S of FRACAS up two places, giving FRASCA; 'backing' turns IT into TI.
explanation.definitionFit: Frascati is a white wine from the hills near Rome, so it is a drink.

clue.text: Hidden muscles and a pair of triceps put to some purpose

parts.note: abs are abdominal muscles

indicators.note: a pair of means the first two letters of triceps are taken

parts.note: to use something is to put it to some purpose

explanation.surface: A gym-goer working abdominals and triceps for some reason.
explanation.definitionFit: Abstruse means obscure, its meaning concealed from ordinary understanding.

clue.text: Pregnant woman, perhaps eating a Mexican meal

indicators.note: eating means the woman takes the letter a inside

parts.note: a woman named Ena (as in Ena Sharples of Coronation Street) holding a child inside her, so pregnant

explanation.surface: An expectant mother tucking into Mexican food.
explanation.walkthrough: ENA is a woman's name; with CHILD inside she is pregnant, ENCHILDA, and 'eating' puts A inside the CHILD part.
explanation.definitionFit: An enchilada is a rolled tortilla with a filling, a classic Mexican dish.

clue.text: Weirdos in daze about netting lawsuit

indicators.note: netting means catching the lawsuit word inside
about turns the daze word round

parts.note: to daze someone is to stun them
a case is a lawsuit brought in court

explanation.surface: Strange people bewildered by a legal action caught up around them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns STUN into NUTS, which nets CASE.
explanation.definitionFit: Nutcases is slang for crazy or eccentric people, oddballs.

clue.text: Famous quotation contradicted in part of the British Isles

definitions.text: Famous quotation contradicted in part of the British Isles

parts.words: Famous quotation contradicted in part of the British Isles
parts.note: John Donne's line says no person stands alone, yet on the Isle of Man the place itself is called Man, and Man is an island

explanation.surface: A well-known saying proved wrong somewhere in Britain or Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Man sits in the Irish Sea, so there Man literally is an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Donne's meditation line, a much-quoted saying that every person is connected to others.

clue.text: Marx pulled up your plant

parts.note: Chico Marx, one of the Marx Brothers

indicators.note: pulled up, in a down clue, means reading the abbreviation from bottom to top

parts.note: YR is a written abbreviation for your

explanation.surface: A Marx, perhaps Karl, tugging up someone's plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicory is a blue-flowered plant grown for salad leaves and its root.

clue.text: As a result of which Oxford could be closed

definitions.text: As a result of which Oxford could be closed

parts.words: As a result of which Oxford could be closed
parts.note: an Oxford is a style of shoe fastened by tying a cord, not the university

explanation.surface: Something that could shut down the famous university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oxford' wants to be the university; it is a laced shoe.
explanation.definitionFit: A cord threaded through eyelets that ties a shoe such as an Oxford closed.

clue.text: Pretend diamond is a national symbol

parts.note: sham means pretend, fake
rock is slang for a diamond

explanation.surface: A fake gem passed off as an emblem of the nation.
explanation.definitionFit: The three-leaved clover is the emblem of Ireland.

clue.text: Better rock music — potentially hot stuff

parts.note: to cap something is to better or outdo it

indicators.note: rock means shake, so the letters of music are shaken up

explanation.surface: A claim that this rock music is superior and could be red-hot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rock' looks like a genre of music; it is the anagram signal for 'music'.
explanation.definitionFit: Capsicum is the pepper genus, including chillies that can be fiery.

clue.text: Buck's Fizz intend to make comeback around short greatest number

indicators.note: around means the reversed word goes round the shortened word
to make a comeback here means the intend word runs backwards

parts.note: to aim is to intend

indicators.note: short means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: most means the greatest number

explanation.surface: A cocktail bar plan for a comeback, measured in drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buck's Fizz' is the British name for the drink Americans call a mimosa; 'greatest number' is an adjective trimmed by one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Mimosa is the American name for the champagne and orange juice cocktail.

clue.text: Stingy character is for going round to stop heir

indicators.note: to stop means plugging a gap, so the reversed word goes inside

parts.note: a scion is a descendant or heir

indicators.note: going round means the for word is turned backwards

parts.note: pro means for, as in being for something

explanation.surface: A mean figure determined to block an heir from inheriting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stingy' suggests a miser; it means having a sting.
explanation.definitionFit: A scorpion is a creature with a venomous tail sting.

clue.text: People are chopping every English tree

indicators.note: chopping every means removing each occurrence of the letter from the phrase

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for English, here standing for each E

explanation.surface: Folk felling every English tree in sight.
explanation.walkthrough: Take PEOPLE ARE and remove all three Es.
explanation.definitionFit: The poplar is a tall, fast-growing deciduous tree.

clue.text: Scattered property in boxes, about to leave urban area

parts.note: to spar is to box, as in practice fighting

indicators.note: to leave means taking the about letter out

parts.note: a city is an urban area
C stands for circa, about

explanation.surface: An estate agent's blurb for scattered property, with crates involved, leaving town.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparsity is thinness of spread, the quality of being thinly scattered.

clue.text: Overpowering sort, lacking exercise, chased talent

indicators.note: lacking means the exercise letters are dropped

parts.note: a type is a sort
PE is physical education, exercise
ran as in chased after
nous is good sense or aptitude

explanation.surface: A domineering type who skipped the gym but pursued talent.
explanation.definitionFit: Tyrannous describes despotic, oppressive behaviour.

clue.text: Cardinal that contributes to every part of Voluntary Service Overseas

parts.words: that contributes to every part of Voluntary Service Overseas
parts.note: each of the three words of the charity's name contains a V, the Roman numeral for this number

explanation.surface: A senior churchman helping with every branch of the volunteer charity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cardinal' suggests a churchman; it is a counting number. VSO is a British overseas volunteering charity.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardinal numbers are counting numbers, and this is one of them.

clue.text: Turn overlooked by sly governor

indicators.note: in a down entry, overlooked by means the other word sits above

parts.note: fly is slang for sly, knowing
to wheel is to turn

explanation.surface: A crafty governor whose turn passed unnoticed.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy wheel that regulates an engine's speed acts as a governor.

clue.text: Whizz kids regularly tour around with very ordinary clothing

indicators.note: clothing means the two letters wrap round the rest
around means the letters are moved about
regularly means every other letter of kids is taken

explanation.surface: Children on a tour dressed in very plain outfits.
explanation.walkthrough: Unusually, the regular selection from 'kids' happens inside the anagram fodder before 'around' mixes it with the tour letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A whizz is an expert, someone dazzlingly skilled.

clue.text: Duration of feeble broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means spoken out, so we hear the feeble word

parts.note: weak means feeble

explanation.surface: How long a poor broadcast lasts.
explanation.definitionFit: Seven days is a span of time, a duration.

clue.text: Fleece heartless old crone somewhere in London

parts.note: a fleece is a sheep's wool

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letter is removed

parts.note: a witch is an old crone

explanation.surface: Swindling a cruel old woman somewhere in the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fleece' looks like a verb meaning to cheat; it is the noun. Woolwich is a district of south-east London.
explanation.definitionFit: Woolwich is a district on the south bank of the Thames in London.

clue.text: Cheesed off about north European city

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters surround the north letter
off means spoilt or upset, so the letters are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: Someone fed up about a city in northern Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'north European' reads as one phrase; 'north' gives N.
explanation.definitionFit: Enschede is a city in the eastern Netherlands.

clue.text: Doctor is noble, hiding nothing having run into trouble

indicators.note: hiding means the nothing letter is concealed, taken from view

parts.note: a baron is a noble
O looks like zero, nothing

indicators.note: into means the run letter goes inside

parts.note: ado is fuss or trouble
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A doctor who is a nobleman, empty-handed after running into difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Barnardo was the doctor who founded children's homes in Victorian Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Dr Thomas Barnardo, founder of the children's charity bearing his name.

clue.text: Red symbol shielded in part

indicators.note: in part says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A communist emblem partly protected.
explanation.definitionFit: Bolshie is informal for Bolshevik, a revolutionary communist, a Red.

clue.text: Turkey has one western Prime Minister shunning a European

indicators.note: shunning means leaving one letter out

parts.note: Clement Attlee was the UK Prime Minister from 1945 to 1951
E is short for European, and a means just one of them

explanation.surface: Turkey's western-leaning leader avoiding a European partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turkey' suggests the country; it is the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A turkey has a fleshy red lobe of skin hanging from its throat.

clue.text: Browning is thwarted by this daily embargo

parts.note: The Sun is a British daily newspaper
a block is a ban or embargo

explanation.surface: A poet named Browning silenced by a newspaper ban.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital makes 'Browning' look like the poet; it means tanning. The Sun is a British daily tabloid.
explanation.definitionFit: A cream that shields skin from the sun's rays and so prevents tanning.

clue.text: Champion immersed in unlimited calm for ages

indicators.note: immersed in means placed inside
unlimited means the outer letters are taken away

parts.note: repose is calm, rest

explanation.surface: A winner sunk in endless calm for a long time.
explanation.definitionFit: Epochs are long eras of history, periods spanning ages.

clue.text: It makes things fine for old Scrooge

parts.note: at can mean for, as in sold at a price
Ebenezer Scrooge, Dickens's miser

explanation.surface: Something that improves matters for the old skinflint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fine' suggests good; it means a fine spray.
explanation.definitionFit: A spray device breaks liquid into very small droplets, making it fine.

clue.text: Unfinished work of son in Cornish town having to stop

indicators.note: in means the son letter goes inside

parts.note: Looe is a fishing town in Cornwall, in south-west England
to end is to stop

explanation.surface: A son's job left undone in a Cornish town that must halt.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose end is a detail left unresolved, a job not yet finished.

clue.text: Dropped off, mainly outside church, in drag

indicators.note: outside means wrapping round the church letters
mainly means most of it, losing the last letter

parts.note: to drop off is to fall asleep, so slept

explanation.surface: Someone who dozed off outside church dressed in drag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in drag' suggests cross-dressing; 'drag' is a tiresome haul.
explanation.definitionFit: To schlep is to drag or haul something heavy and awkward.
